available_years.note: 2026 is provisional (~3 MB, basic boundaries only, no buurt/wijk). Historical editions 1995-2015 were previously available.

gegeneraliseerd.description_en: Generalized (simplified) polygons suitable for thematic mapping at national/regional scales

niet_gegeneraliseerd.description_en: Non-generalized (detailed) polygons with precise boundaries, available only for gemeente, wijk, and buurt

labelpoint.description_en: Centroid points for cartographic labeling, one per polygon feature

area_classifications.description: Primary local government unit. The fundamental building block of all Dutch administrative geography.
Sub-municipal districts. Each gemeente is subdivided into wijken for statistical purposes.
Neighborhoods, the finest-grained CBS statistical unit. Each wijk is subdivided into buurten.
The 12 Dutch provinces, the primary regional government level between national and municipal.
Four macro-regions: Noord-Nederland, Oost-Nederland, West-Nederland, Zuid-Nederland.
Regions where labour supply and demand are geographically matched. Used for employment policy and UWV (employee insurance) administration.
Alternative labour market regional classification used by the RegioPlus network of regional labour market organizations.
Jurisdictional areas of the 11 district courts (rechtbanken) in the Dutch judicial system.
Jurisdictional areas of the 4 courts of appeal (gerechtshoven): Amsterdam, Arnhem-Leeuwarden, Den Haag, 's-Hertogenbosch.
Regions defined by the Coordinatiecommissie Regionaal Onderzoeksprogramma. The standard classification for regional economic analysis, roughly comparable to NUTS-3.
Subdivisions of COROP regions for finer-grained regional economic analysis.
Extended COROP classification with additional subdivisions for metropolitan areas.
Regions responsible for coordinating fire services, disaster response, crisis management, and medical emergency services.
Service areas of the Gemeentelijke Gezondheidsdienst (Municipal Health Services) responsible for public health, epidemiology, and preventive care.
Regions for organizing youth care (jeugdzorg) services, established after the 2015 decentralization of youth services to municipalities.
Regions of health insurance offices (zorgkantoren) that administer long-term care (Wlz) on behalf of health insurers.
Service areas for Veilig Thuis organizations that handle reports of domestic violence and child abuse.
Operational units of the Dutch National Police, established in the 2013 police reorganization.
Regions for combating school dropout, where RMC coordinators track and support early school leavers.
Regions designated under the National Climate Agreement for coordinating the energy transition at regional level.
Sub-regions within RES areas for more localized energy transition planning.
Regions of the Dutch Chamber of Commerce (KvK) for business registration and economic services.
Fine-grained agricultural classification areas for farm statistics and agricultural policy analysis.
Aggregated groupings of agricultural areas sharing similar farming characteristics and landscape types.
Regions classified for tourism statistics and analysis of visitor patterns.
Higher-level aggregation of tourist areas by tourism type (e.g., coastal, nature, urban, watersport).

gebiedsindelingen_register.description_en: A lookup/crosswalk table with 342 rows (one per gemeente) mapping each municipality to ALL of its parent area classifications. Contains code and name columns for every classification type (gm_, am_, ar_, cr_, cs_, cp_, gg_, jz_, kk_, lb_, lg_, ld_, re_, pv_, ra_, es_, rt_, mc_, et_, tr_, tg_, vt_, vr_, zk_).
gebiedsindelingen_register.description_nl: Een koppeltabel die elke gemeente koppelt aan alle gebiedsindelingen waartoe deze behoort.

statcode.description: CBS statistical code, unique within classification type (e.g., 'GM0014', 'PV20', 'VR01')

jrstatcode.description: Year-prefixed statistical code for temporal disambiguation (e.g., '2025GM0014', '2025PV20')

non_generalized_layers.note: Same columns as generalized, but wijk and buurt layers add gm_code (String) linking the feature to its parent gemeente.

gm_code.description: Parent gemeente code (e.g., 'GM0014'), present on wijk and buurt non-generalized layers

context.what: The single most comprehensive official source of Dutch regional boundary classifications. While Bestuurlijke Gebieden provides precise administrative boundaries and CBS Wijken en Buurten adds demographic statistics, Gebiedsindelingen is the authoritative reference that defines ALL regional classification systems used in Dutch governance and statistics.
context.why_important: The Netherlands uses over 25 distinct regional classification systems for different government functions. Every policy domain — from healthcare to policing, energy transition to tourism — has its own regional subdivision. This dataset is the Rosetta Stone that maps between them all, anchored to the 342 gemeenten as the fundamental unit.
common_uses: Thematic mapping of statistics by any regional classification
Joining CBS statistical tables (StatLine) to geographic boundaries
Cross-referencing between classification systems (e.g., which veiligheidsregio does a gemeente belong to?)
Policy analysis requiring geographic aggregation at different scales
Building web maps showing Dutch administrative and functional regions
Temporal analysis of how regional boundaries change year over year

related_datasets.name: CBS Wijken en Buurten
related_datasets.relationship: Adds demographic/socioeconomic statistics (population, income, housing, etc.) to the buurt/wijk/gemeente boundaries that are also in Gebiedsindelingen

related_datasets.name: Bestuurlijke Gebieden (Kadaster)
related_datasets.relationship: Provides legally precise administrative boundaries (gemeente/provincie/land) from the Kadaster. Gebiedsindelingen uses CBS-defined generalized boundaries instead.

related_datasets.name: CBS StatLine
related_datasets.relationship: The national statistics database whose tables can be joined to Gebiedsindelingen boundaries via statcode/jrstatcode
